summary: S1 labels 43 genes up and 38 down, while the manuscript reports 45 up and 38 down. The first author’s thesis lists only the first 63 S1 genes, and the published volcano plot supports a nominal-P threshold. The named gene effects meet author-concordance-v2, but the public records leave the two additional upregulated genes and the original calling code unresolved.

manualReview.summary: Emulsifier effects agree across the named S1 results. Two reported upregulated genes remain unidentified.
manualReview.note: For the registered P21 male MBH contrast, PLOS S1 and its Europe PMC and PLOS Figshare copies are byte-identical. Rows 65–173 have no values and one further statistical row has no gene ID. All 14,483 named S1 genes match uniquely to the registered output of 14,592 genes. Among these pairs, Pearson r is 0.991707, Spearman rho is 0.995943, and 14,195 have the same direction. Both author-concordance-v2 routes pass for paired gene effects. The registered coefficients reproduce the GEO matrix's case-minus-control group means within 4.6e-14 log2 units. The paper reports 45 up and 38 down. S1 labels 43 up and 38 down, and the first author’s thesis Annex 1 prints only the first 63 named S1 rows. All 63 labels agree and the largest absolute difference in their reported logFC values is below 5e-9. Figure 3A plots raw P and shows logFC guides at approximately ±0.65. On named S1 rows, raw P < 0.05 and |logFC| > 0.65 reproduce the labels exactly. The original code is unavailable. Applying the methods’ nominal P and 1.5-fold rule gives 109 author and 87 registered calls on shared finite rows, with 85 in common. Applying the caption’s FDR and 1.5-fold rule gives zero in either table. For FDR < 0.05 alone, both registered calls are among five author calls. Mylk4 adds one nominal-P/1.5-fold registered call without an author row. Its author inference and that of the other unmatched genes remain unassessed.
reviewFlags: S1 has 109 empty row positions and one result without an identifier. Author effect and inference remain unavailable for 109 named registered genes.
The article reports two more upregulated genes than S1 labels. The thesis annex supplies a shorter list and the figure-data DOI returns HTTP 404.
The caption, methods and S1 imply different significance rules. The original fit and figure code remain unavailable.

verificationReview.reason: The registered comparison passes both v2 effect-concordance routes across 14,483 named pairs. S1 supplies 81 labels, the thesis annex repeats 63 of those rows, and the paper reports 83. The plot and S1 support nominal P, while the caption specifies FDR. An unlabelled raster, expression inputs and incomplete author tables cannot identify the two additional upregulated genes or authenticate the fitted model.
verificationReview.nextStep: Was the reported count of 45 upregulated genes a counting error? If it was correct, which two additional genes were counted, and can the authors provide the complete keyed limma output and the analysis and plotting code that produced Figure 3A, including the normalization, design or weights, P-value column and logFC cutoff?

comparabilityReview.basis: Direct comparison of the current registered limma output with every named row of the near-complete S1 table. The published figure and the selected thesis annex were checked separately to investigate the reported DEG count.
comparabilityReview.reference: PLOS S1, Differentially Expressed Genes worksheet. Secondary selected reference from Milà Guasch, Annex 1, printed pages 109–110.

cohort.note: GEO family SOFT, the registered sample sheet and the manuscript identify four control and five exposed litters, male P21 MBH. Each registered library represents an offspring from a different litter.

contrast.note: P21 male mediobasal hypothalamus, maternal CMC plus P80 versus control water. S1 Up and Down denote change in exposed offspring. The registered coefficient uses groupcase with control as baseline.

features.note: All 14,483 unique named S1 identifiers join exactly to registered IDs. The workbook’s unnamed result has no auditable gene mapping.

effects.note: Both estimates describe maternal emulsifier minus control in log2 units. Pearson r = 0.991707, Spearman rho = 0.995943, same direction in 14,195/14,483 nonzero pairs, median absolute logFC difference = 0.004021. The registered group-mean contrast reproduces directly from GEO.

inference.note: S1 has five and the registered output two FDR < 0.05 calls among shared finite genes, with both registered calls in common. S1 labels follow the empirical nominal P and |logFC| > 0.65 rule. Neither stated 1.5-fold rule yields the published count. The authors describe limma but supply no original call-generating code in the sources reviewed.

coverage.note: 14,483/14,592 registered genes have paired finite results (99.253%). All named S1 genes are covered. The other 109 local genes, including Mylk4, lack author statistics. Every one of the 63 selected thesis genes is already in S1.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use case minus control with exact unique gene IDs. For a full table, evaluate v2 against all registered genes, require at least 30 pairs and 90% coverage, then evaluate the alternative correlation and nonzero-direction routes. Assess raw P and FDR separately on shared finite results and account for registered calls outside that set. Test the caption and methods as written. The earlier 0.65 observation describes S1 and was checked against the figure.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: Both v2 routes pass for paired gene effects. Full reproduction remains unresolved because of the unidentified upregulated genes, the omitted results and the uncertainty about the original inference.
